correctness.rationale: Replayed the proof for the repaired claim n≥5 (the frozen argument is also valid at n=4). Ordered torus pair sums collide beyond permutation only on the three perfect matchings of four distinct vertices. Hence the diagonal baseline is 2S²−sum x_e² and the extra term is eight times the sum of real cross products of the matching coefficient products. Triangle and the three-variable squared-difference inequality bound this term by 8 times the sum over disjoint unordered pairs. Alternatively, each four-cycle product is bounded by a quarter of the sum over its four adjacent pairs by AM–GM; across the three cycles each adjacent pair appears once per quadruple and n−3 times globally, giving the factor 2(n−3). Both estimates are exact on constant positive coefficients. Combining with disjoint weight (n−4)/(n−1) gives H=−I+4αK+(n−3)(1−α)L. Incidence B gives L=BᵀB−2I and BBᵀ=(n−2)I+J, so L has eigenvalues 2(n−2), n−4, −2 on constants, the incidence differences and the kernel. With K=J−I−L, these give h₀=−1+2(n−2)(n−3), h₁=−1−(n−3)(n−4)/(n−1), h₂=−3. Projecting x onto constants proves the displayed remainder and its coefficient values. The argument includes all zero entries. For the frozen equality claim, the strict spectral gap first makes magnitudes positive and equal; matching products must then agree as complex numbers on every quadruple. Choosing u₁²=a₁₂a₁₃/a₂₃ after modulus normalization and u_j=a₁j/u₁ recovers every edge via the quadruples. This qualitative theorem is context in the repair. I also verified the comparison statement for unit coefficient: in the all-layer balancing proof the doubled-monomial gap is 6((b²+c²)/2)²−(b⁴+c⁴+4b²c²)=(b²−c²)²/2. This equals the decrease in squared dispersion of that pair. Repeated cyclic transposition averages are orthogonal projections on the edge-energy vector; their full-cycle product is strictly contracting away from constants (norm equality would require membership in every fixed subspace), so telescoping establishes the comparison for the whole vector.
residual_risks: The frozen checker supplies finite corroboration only. The repaired global magnitude coefficient is certified but not claimed optimal; no phase stability bound is asserted.

value.rationale: The complete homogeneous degree-two layer is a standard natural coefficient space. The quantitative inequality gives explicit global near-maximizer control on all squared magnitudes, even when some vanish. It strengthens the unit-coefficient balancing control from 1 to 3 in every dimension n≥7 by exploiting the two complete-graph pair types, rather than changing notation or extracting a small instance. This is a separate useful estimate; the repair makes no new claim to the qualitative sharp norm or phase orbit.
residual_risks: The improvement is confined to magnitude dispersion in the complete degree-two layer, and does not control arbitrary coefficient phase distance.
